samples.summary: The whole feature is unreachable on the shipped dependency pin, so none of the design's Goals are met by this change
samples.evidence: `MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"` and `supportsClientKey()` reads `__YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__`, which `vite.config.ts` injects from `packages/frontend/package.json` — pinned at `"@yorkie-js/react": "0.7.22"` (line 66). So `supportsClientKey()` is false in every build produced by this branch. That gate hides the Settings switch (`app/settings/page.tsx`: `{offlineAvailable && ...}`), hides the chip's offer (`offerOffline = stranded && supportsClientKey() && ...`), and refuses durability in `useDurableDocument`. The result is that 'edits made while disconnected survive a reload', 'the sync chip tells the truth about durability', and 'work that cannot be reconciled is returned as a document' — the four Goals at the top of `docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md` — are unachievable by any user on this branch. The design doc acknowledges this ('PR 4 lands inert... the Goals at the top of this document are unmet until the dependency is bumped'), so it is deliberate, but it means the acceptance of this PR cannot rest on observed behavior: every user-facing promise is dark until a separate dependency bump. Worth an explicit decision rather than an implicit one, since the reviewable surface here is wiring only.

samples.summary: The `Not saved` tooltip never names why durability lapsed, which the design states as a requirement of the new state
samples.evidence: `docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md` § What the user sees gives a six-row table mapping each cause to a distinct tooltip ('Open in another tab; that one is saving', 'This browser cannot save locally', 'Too large to save on this device', 'Out of local storage space', 'Could not save to this device') and then states: 'Because `Not saved` is now a *designed* state rather than the only state — the second tab, an oversized document, a broken store — ... Its tooltip must name which case applies.' The Risks table repeats it ('Its tooltip names the reason'). `tooltipFor`'s `not-saved` arm implements only a connected/disconnected split plus the opt-in offer; nothing in the chip consumes `persistDisabled`, the store's `onWriteFailure` reason, or the lost-election fact. A user in the second tab of a document with the preference ON — a case this design newly creates — sees the destructive 'Not saved' with 'They exist only in this tab' and no indication that the other tab is saving, and no offer either (`offerOffline` requires `!offlineEnabled`). That defeats the stated purpose of making `durable` a first-class signal rather than a cosmetic one.

samples.summary: The design doc states archives stay user-scoped in the 30-day sweep; the implementation deliberately does the opposite
samples.evidence: The doc says: 'Archives stay scoped: another account's is the only copy of work their SDK could not reconcile, and it is theirs to collect.' `WafflebaseDocStore.collectStale` calls `this.dropArchivesWhere(BY_ARCHIVED_AT, range)` with no `onlyUser` argument (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1129), and its own comment argues at length for the reverse ('Archives are swept on exactly the same terms... scoping the sweep to this user left another account's content with no collection path at all'), with `wafflebase-doc-store-cleanup.test.ts` asserting another account's stale archive is collected. Doc and code in the same diff contradict each other on a data-retention rule; `dropArchivesWhere`'s `onlyUser` parameter is now unreachable. The code's reasoning looks like the later decision, so the doc sentence is the stale half.

samples.summary: The design claims the recovery path reuses the existing copy engine (`DocumentCopyService` / `POST /documents/:id/copy`); it does not touch it
samples.evidence: § Losing work anyway: 'we already have the machinery for it in `DocumentCopyService` / `POST /documents/:id/copy`', and See Also lists `document-copy.md` as 'the copy engine the offline-copy recovery path reuses'. `lib/offline-copy-recovery.ts` uses `createDocument` + `applyImportedContent` (and a bespoke `writeNote`), and never calls `copyDocument`/`copyDocuments` from `api/documents.ts`. The implementation choice is defensible — the copy endpoint duplicates a server-side document and the source here is local bytes the server never saw — but the doc asserts a reuse relationship that does not exist, which is exactly the kind of claim a reader later builds on.

samples.summary: `writeNote` re-implements `applyImportedContent`'s Yorkie client lifecycle in `lib/` instead of adding a `note` branch to the repo's canonical apply seam
samples.evidence: `applyImportedContent` (app/documents/apply-imported-content.ts:228) is the existing per-type seam: one `new Client({rpcAddr, apiKey, authTokenInjector: fetchYorkieToken})`, `activate()` outside the try, per-type `attach` → write → `detach`, `deactivate()` in `finally`, with `buildDocKey` owning key construction. `writeNote` copies that lifecycle verbatim (down to the 'activate() outside the try' rationale) and rebuilds the key as `note-${docId}` by hand. The repo's stated expectation is reuse; a `note` case in `ImportedContent` would have kept one client-lifecycle implementation and one docKey rule. As written the two will drift — the apply seam's docblock already warns that per-type root writes must be kept in step with the editor mount paths, and this second writer is outside that warning's reach.

samples.summary: The README index row for `sync-status.md` still states offline persistence is deferred, contradicting the doc it summarises after this change
samples.evidence: The `sync-status.md` row ends: 'Offline persistence deferred — `@yorkie-js/sdk@0.7.20` added an opt-in `ClientOptions.store` but we pass none, and turning it on needs a stable `clientKey`... which is why the wording never claims local durability'. This diff rewrites `sync-status.md` to un-defer exactly that (the Non-Goal is struck through, a fifth `saved-locally` state is added, the unload guard is suppressed when durable). The index is the repo's map of which doc is canonical for what; leaving this row asserting the reversed position is the duplicate-source-of-truth problem the design-doc discipline exists to avoid. The new row for `offline-local-persistence.md` was added correctly; only the neighbouring row was left stale.

samples.summary: The offline-transition toast is dropped entirely on a durable document, where the design specifies changed wording
samples.evidence: § What the user sees: 'Two consequences follow automatically: the `beforeunload` guard is suppressed when `durable`, and the offline-transition toast changes from "keep this tab open" to "saved to this device".' The guard suppression is implemented (`mayHaveUnsent = stranded || state === 'saving'`, and `saved-locally` is neither). The toast is not: the warning effect is keyed on `stranded`, so a durable document going offline produces no toast at all, and `sync-status-chip.test.tsx` pins that absence (`expect(warning).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`). Defensible as a muting decision, but it is a divergence from a behaviour the design states as following 'automatically', and it means the user is never actively told their work landed on disk — only the ambient chip says so.

samples.summary: The recovery notification does not use 'the vocabulary of the three reasons' the design specifies, because the loss reason is discarded
samples.evidence: § Losing work anyway: 'The user is then told what happened, in the vocabulary of the three reasons, with a link to the copy' — i.e. `epoch-reanchor` (force-compacted), `document-purged` (deleted upstream), `actor-mismatch` (another identity). `DurableLossWatch` subscribes to `local-changes-dropped` and calls `durable.store.expectLoss(doc.getKey())` without reading `event.value.reason`; `ArchiveRecord` stores no reason; `offerRecoverableWork` emits one generic 'could not be reconciled with the server'. The three cases call for materially different user action (the `document-purged` case in particular means the original is gone), so collapsing them loses information the design asked to be surfaced.

samples.summary: `documentIdOf` duplicates the exported `documentKeyOf`, and `describeArchivedDocument` re-implements the same split a third time
samples.evidence: `wafflebase-doc-store.ts` exports `documentKeyOf(key)` with a docblock saying it lives there precisely because 'two copies of the rule is how the guard that matched a lock name against a store key came to be silently false'. `offline-copy.ts` then defines a private `documentIdOf` with the identical body, and `offline-copy-recovery.ts:describeArchivedDocument` splits on `/` and takes the last segment again. Three copies of one rule, in the same feature, one of which already has a comment explaining why duplicating it is dangerous.

verdict.reason: The factual evidence checks out: MinClientKeyVersion is "0.7.23" (packages/frontend/src/lib/yorkie-capabilities.ts:24), supportsClientKey() reads __YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__ (:76-82), vite.config.ts:414-418 injects it from packages/frontend/package.json:66 which pins "@yorkie-js/react": "0.7.22", and the gate suppresses the Settings switch (app/settings/page.tsx:35,111), the chip offer (sync-status-chip.tsx:146) and the durable client (collab-document-provider.tsx:196). So the feature is indeed dark on this branch. It is not blocking under the design-fit lens, however, because this is precisely what the governing spec prescribes rather than a deviation from it: docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:497-507 states "PR 4 lands inert, and stays inert until one upstream release … the Goals at the top of this document are unmet until the dependency is bumped. Bumping it is the whole remaining action — no code here changes with it — and until then what is being reviewed and tested is the wiring, not the behavior," and :193-197 requires both opt-in entry points to sit behind supportsClientKey() exactly so a build that cannot persist does not offer storage and erasure. The branch's own task plan says the same (docs/tasks/active/20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md:36-41, 119, 220, 242-246). The change therefore conforms to its spec; no acceptance criterion for this PR is left unmet, no logic is duplicated, no Non-Goal is crossed, and the design doc exists and is current. The finding's stated remedy — that the deferral be an explicit decision rather than an implicit one — is already discharged in writing at those locations plus in-code rationale at app/settings/page.tsx:97-110 and yorkie-capabilities.ts:59-75. Under the rubric this is a deferred-value/sequencing observation whose cost stays inside the codebase, i.e. minor at most, and minor never blocks.

verdict.reason: The absence is real and I could not find a counterexample. `tooltipFor`'s `not-saved` arm (sync-status-chip.tsx:91-122) produces only a connected/disconnected split, a fixed "exists only in this tab" sentence, and the opt-in offer; nothing names the second-tab election, `PersistDisabled`, quota exhaustion, or store write failure. Those causes exist as three separate latches in durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:92-166 but are collapsed into a single boolean at line 154, and durable-document-context.ts:20-76 publishes only `durable: boolean` — so no reason can reach the chip; sync-state.ts:24-49 likewise carries no discriminant. The design states the requirement twice as a must (offline-local-persistence.md:425-430 table, :441-444 "Its tooltip must name which case applies", :519 Risks mitigation). The branch's own task list corroborates it is undone: 20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md:91-94 leaves item 3.4 ("A typed reason for the tooltip wording") unchecked, noting the `DurabilityLapse` type was written and removed pending "the tooltip that needs it". Two qualifications, neither sufficient to refute: (1) row 1 of the design table (preference off -> offer to turn it on) IS implemented at sync-status-chip.tsx:118-119, so "never names why" is overstated for the default case; (2) the durable client is currently unreachable (yorkie-capabilities.ts:24,76-82 with package.json:66 pinning @yorkie-js/react 0.7.22), so rows 2-6 cannot occur today. That second point would argue for lower severity, except the design (:507) and yorkie-capabilities.ts:67 both promise the dependency bump is the *only* remaining action with "no code here changes with it" — which this gap falsifies, keeping it inside PR 4's declared scope rather than a legitimate follow-up.

finding.summary: `durable` omits the `PersistDisabled` conjunct the design specifies, so a document the SDK stopped persisting can still report "Saved to this device"
finding.evidence: docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md § What the user sees: "`durable` is the conjunction of three facts: this tab won the app lock, no `PersistDisabled` event has latched this document off, and the store is not failing its writes", and the table row "Document too large / too slow to snapshot | false | Too large to save on this device". The implementation latches only on `local-changes-dropped` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:181) and `onWriteFailure`; `sync-state.ts:44` names `PersistDisabled` in a comment but nothing subscribes to it. A grep across packages/frontend/src for `PersistDisabled|persist-disabled` returns only that comment. If the SDK disables persistence for an oversized document, the chip keeps promising local durability — the one direction the design says must never fail.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `durable` omits the `PersistDisabled` conjunct and that nothing subscribes to the event. Both parts are false in this tree. `durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:154` computes `durable: !lost && !writesFailing && !persistDisabled`, with the latch state and `reportPersistDisabled` callback declared at lines 106-110 and documented at lines 95-105 as "The second of the design's three conjuncts." The subscription the reviewer says does not exist is at `durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:227-229` inside `DurableLossWatch`: `doc.subscribe('persist-disabled', () => durable.reportPersistDisabled())`, cleaned up at line 232 — the reviewer likely missed it because the event is spelled kebab-case alongside the `local-changes-dropped` subscription at line 217. The context surface carries it at `durable-document-context.ts:39`. The reviewer's claimed grep result ("returns only that comment") does not reproduce: the same pattern returns nine source hits plus tests that emit the event (`durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx:115,128`) and assert it is subscribed (`__tests__/collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:376`). The design's three-conjunct definition is therefore implemented and the "too large to snapshot -> false" row is reachable; there is no spec-conformance gap of the kind described.

finding.summary: The whole feature is unreachable on the pinned SDK: `@yorkie-js/react` is 0.7.22 while `MinClientKeyVersion` is 0.7.23, so `supportsClientKey()` is false and both opt-in entry points are hidden
finding.evidence: packages/frontend/package.json pins `"@yorkie-js/react": "0.7.22"`; yorkie-capabilities.ts sets `MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"` and `supportsClientKey()` gates the Settings switch (app/settings/page.tsx), the chip offer, and `useDurableDocument`'s eligibility. As shipped, no user can opt in, so the design's primary Goal — "Edits made while disconnected survive a reload ... on a device where the user has asked for it" — is unreachable on this build. The design anticipates the gate ("Bumping the dependency is the only action needed"), but the Rollout section describes PR 4 as a dark launch "bounded by who turned it on", which presumes somebody can.

verdict.reason: The code facts are as described (package.json:66 pins 0.7.22; yorkie-capabilities.ts:24 requires 0.7.23; the gate covers settings/chip/provider), but the finding's blocking premise — that the design presumes somebody can opt in on this build — is contradicted by the same Rollout section it cites. docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:497-507 states verbatim "PR 4 lands inert, and stays inert until one upstream release… Nobody on the shipped pin can turn the feature on… the Goals at the top of this document are unmet until the dependency is bumped. Bumping it is the whole remaining action — no code here changes with it — and until then what is being reviewed and tested is the wiring, not the behavior." The originating task doc agrees and does not claim the behavior as delivered: lines 38-41 ("the feature is dark rather than absent"), line 220 leaves "Manual smoke — needs the dependency bump" unchecked, and lines 242-246 record the durable client as "still unreachable, and deliberately". The upstream 0.7.23 release is documented as not yet published. Therefore the inert state is the specified outcome of this change, not an unmet acceptance criterion or scope miss under the design-fit lens.
